issues.legal_issue: A government that proceeds with acquisition under the general acquisition law cannot use a reference seeking enhanced compensation to raise an adverse claim that the landholders’ interests had vested in it under a separate abolition process.
material_facts: The land was notified under both the acquisition law and the estate abolition law.
Proceedings under the abolition law were stayed, while acquisition proceedings continued.
The landholders sought a reference to challenge the compensation awarded to them.
The government’s claim that the landholders had lost their interests was raised only in the appeal from the reference decision.
issues.conclusion: The government could not raise its adverse claim in that reference, and the rejection of the claim was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The government had alternative routes: proceed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, or take over the land under the Madras Estates Abolition Act, 1948. Because the abolition proceedings were stayed and the matter proceeded under the Land Acquisition Act, compensation had to be determined under that Act. The reference under section 18 concerned the quantum payable to claimants whose interest in the land was the underlying assumption of the proceedings. The government had to take appropriate steps to assert any claim that the claimants’ interests had vested in it; it could not set up that adverse claim in the particular reference. No earlier case is identified by name.

rule.if: acquisition_compensation_appeal and abolition_proceeding_stayed and acquisition_proceeding_continued and landholders_sought_quantum_reference and divestment_claim_first_raised_on_appeal

predicates.acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation determined in acquisition proceedings.
predicates.abolition_proceeding_stayed: Proceedings under a separate land-abolition process were stayed.
predicates.acquisition_proceeding_continued: The government continued the acquisition process under the general acquisition law.
predicates.landholders_sought_quantum_reference: The landholders sought a reference to challenge the amount of compensation awarded to them.
predicates.divestment_claim_first_raised_on_appeal: The government first claimed in the appeal that the landholders had lost their interests in the land.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation appeal follows a stayed abolition process and the landholders sought a reference about quantum, a government that first raises divestment on appeal cannot raise that adverse claim in the reference.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent compensation findings based on an established allocation formula should not be disturbed without cogent grounds for doing so.
material_facts: The lower courts determined compensation for the landholders’ interest by applying a formula adopted in previous decisions.
Under that formula, the landholders were awarded one-half of the compensation payable to the cultivators.
The government showed no cogent ground for interfering with the concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent determination of the compensation amount was left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The courts below applied a formula reflected in previous decisions: one-third of the total compensation was generally allocated to landholders and two-thirds to cultivators, making the landholders’ share one-half of the cultivators’ compensation. In the absence of cogent grounds, the concurrent compensation findings were not disturbed. The judgment identifies no earlier decision by name.

rule.if: compensation_appeal and concurrent_compensation_findings and established_allocation_formula_applied and no_cogent_ground_to_interfere

predicates.compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal challenging compensation determined by lower courts.
predicates.concurrent_compensation_findings: Both lower courts reached the same compensation determination.
predicates.established_allocation_formula_applied: The lower courts used an allocation formula adopted in earlier decisions to divide compensation between landholders and cultivators.
predicates.no_cogent_ground_to_interfere: The appellant showed no cogent ground for disturbing the concurrent determination.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, concurrent findings applying an established allocation formula remain undisturbed when no cogent ground for interference is shown.

issues.legal_issue: Interest on acquisition compensation should not be ordered from a date before the award when the record does not establish that possession was taken earlier.
material_facts: The lower court awarded interest from a date on the basis that possession had been taken then.
The appellate court found no material showing that possession had been taken before the acquisition officer made the award.
The Supreme Court found no reason to disagree with the appellate court’s direction that interest run from the award date.
issues.conclusion: The direction that interest run from the date of the acquisition officer’s award was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The court upheld the appellate court’s determination of the interest commencement date because the record contained no material showing that possession had been taken before the award. The judgment does not identify a statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this determination.

predicates.acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.interest_commencement_disputed: The parties dispute when interest on the compensation should begin.
predicates.no_record_of_possession_before_award: The record contains no material showing that possession was taken before the acquisition award.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation appeal disputes the start of interest and the record does not show possession before the award, interest runs from the award date.
